DEVIATION: Table 1 Model 3 (p. 878). Archived code gives 0.0516 vs the published 0.062 (-16.7%, outside the +/-15% band) on N=12,391 vs 12,066 (+2.7%). Cause: the posted do-file filters Model 3 with 'if outcome == 3'; the paper's Model 3 is 'if earlysettle == 0'. Patched run returns 0.062347 (->0.062), SE 0.136, N=12,066, matching all seven printed coefficients, and Models 2+3 then partition Model 1 exactly (6,027+12,066=18,093; 45+77=122 clusters). Patch is a sample-restriction change, so it is excluded from the headline per the modification policy.

Likely a legend typo for '**p < 0.01' (Model 4's single-starred 0.804 has p=0.018); read that way the claim would be precise. DEVIATION IN N: Table 3 Eq (7), p. 620. NO ANALYSIS CODE WAS POSTED -- only the dataset and a 3-page appendix PDF -- so the model was rebuilt from the published table. Coefficient 0.00732 (->0.007), robust SE 0.00315 (->0.003) and p=0.020 (<0.05) all reproduce exactly, but N=1,739 vs the published 1,718 (+1.22%). The 21 extra observations are every case with tax_rev_new>100, i.e. tax revenue recorded above 100% of total government revenue (Cyprus, Nicaragua, Guatemala, Italy; max 113.0). Dropping them gives N=1,718 exactly and reproduces Eqs (5) and (6) including both pseudo-R2 values, but then the focal coefficient becomes 0.00763 (->0.008). Both readings score approximate. Quadrature settings ruled out (8/12/20/30 integration points agree to 1e-8).

Table 2 Panel A row 1 (p. 714). Effect 0.05, SE 0.02 and N=1,863 reproduce exactly. DEVIATION IN THE RI p-VALUE: paper 0.003 vs reproduced 0.0058 (10,000 reps; MC SE 0.00076; gap = 3.7 MC SEs, so not simulation error). The archived RI re-seeds the RNG inside the simulate loop (blorasim_ri_embed.ado line 91), so its randomization distribution is generated entirely by Stata's sort tie-breaking rather than by the author's design; a repeat run reproduced 0.0058 bit-identically. See REPLICATE_RI_RESULTS.md.

Table 2 Panel A row 2 (p. 714). Effect 0.03, SE 0.02 and N=1,862 reproduce exactly. SIGNIFICANCE FLIP: paper RI p = 0.086 (starred * against the table's own p<0.10 legend) vs reproduced 0.1152, which is ABOVE 0.10 -- the star would disappear and 'weak evidence' would become a null. Gap = 9.2 MC SEs. Robust: a repeat run gave 0.1152 bit-identically and a varied sort tie-break seed gave 0.1082, both still above 0.10. Rubric still scores approximate because 0.1152 is within 0.05 of 0.086.

Table 2 Panel C row 6 (p. 714), votefor_1. Effect 0.04, SE 0.05 and N=458 reproduce exactly. RI p: paper 0.466 vs reproduced 0.4773; gap = 2.3 MC SEs (MC SE 0.00499) -- the only one of Pxp7's five p-value gaps small enough to be ordinary simulation error. Note the archived RI is deterministic within a fixed Stata environment (repeat runs are bit-identical), so 'MC SE' here measures spread across environments/settings, not across runs.

DEVIATION: Table 2 Panel C row 7 (p. 714), votefor_3. Effect -0.03, SE 0.03 and N=458 reproduce exactly, but the RI p-value does not: paper 0.342 vs reproduced 0.2879. The exact-p approximate band is [0.292, 0.392] and 0.2879 falls 0.0041 BELOW the lower bound -> not reproduced. Three independent repeat runs returned 0.2879 bit-identically, so this is not a lucky draw; however, re-running the same unmodified code with Stata's sort tie-break seed varied gives 0.2935 / 0.2872 / 0.2902, and one of those four streams (0.2935) lands inside the band and would score approximate. The verdict is therefore knife-edge and decided by an undocumented Stata sorting setting. See REPLICATE_RI_RESULTS.md. This single claim is what makes the paper-level headline 'not'.

Figure 4 Panel A (p. 718) and text p. 716. The 7-point information effect in the windfall group reproduces exactly (.0686695 -> 7), as does N=1,863 and the tax-group counterpart (.0820389 -> 8). The extraction left the 7-point coefficient as NA even though the paper prints it in text and as a figure label.
